Hub/Care journey/Product screens
Care journey

Product screens.

Step 7 of the assessment and everything after it, in the unifiedmeds system: the recommendation and checkout, the member portal, the provider's clinical admin and support. Every screen at 1440 in a browser frame and at 390 in a phone frame, built from the core components and tokens.

FunnelMember portalClinical adminSupportStatesRules for the developerDecisions
Current · U-29, U-32

Avi's decisions are applied (U-29, U-32). Every name, date, number and message is DEMO data. Square brackets mark what clinical, legal or operations must supply: [DOSE], $[price], [charge line · operations], review and shipping times (R-68), legal lines. The questions, consent, account, ID and Send are designed on Assessment; the funnel here is its step 7.

Decisions applied.

Tadalafil, Sildenafil and Combo (U-21). Product colours mark the product, never text (R-85). Yellow once per screen: the next step, or the funnel's one call to action (R-11). The price only in the checkout card (E-04); plans of 1, 3 and 6 months with no badge (R-61, R-67). The provider-approval line under every treatment option. Disabled at 40% (R-42). Every capsule from tools/capsule_svg.py, with the divider (R-105, R-109).

How to read the frames.

Desktop frames are 1440 wide and scale to fit; phone frames are 390 wide. Frames show the full page height, nothing cropped. Hover and click work: the plan toggles, switches and questions respond.

Funnel: step 7 and after.

One step model for the whole funnel (U-32): the assessment's seven steps, then the provider. Step 7, Plan and send, runs recommendation, checkout, ID and Send, all on the clinical intake domain (R-70). The ID and Send screens are on Assessment.

1 · Recommendation2 · Checkout3 · Sent4 · Provider review

1 · Recommendation.

Step 7 of the assessment opens here, after consent and the account (U-32). One option leads, two alternatives follow, the plan choice and the price card sit together. Plans of 1, 3 and 6 months, no "Most popular" or "Best value" badge (R-61, R-67). The price shows only in the checkout card (E-04). The provider-approval line sits under the options. Product colours mark the products; the text stays Deep Teal. One Yellow element: the checkout button.

Mobile and build notes

  • Order on mobile: title, main option, price card, alternatives, safety information. Nothing is hidden.
  • The bottle tile drops from 250 to 175px tall; alternatives become a single column with a 130px bottle.
  • The sticky bar appears once the price card scrolls out of view; it never covers the safety information heading.
  • Plan choice: the core segmented control with three options (1, 3 and 6 months) and the sliding thumb (220ms). The price lines cross-fade (180ms). No badge on any plan.
  • The saving is said in dollars, "You save $[amount] a month", never as a percentage or a crossed-out price (R-61).
  • Charge line: the placeholder [charge line · operations] until operations decide when and what a member pays (U-31).
  • Wording follows R-64: the provider decides. Never "recommended for you" without the provider line.
  • [DOSE], $[price] and $[amount] stay in brackets until clinical and operations confirm them (R-97, R-61).

2 · Checkout.

Contact, shipping and payment in one page, the order summary beside it. The email comes from the start of the assessment (no password, U-32). Payment fields are UI only. The packaging line sits with the address, where the member thinks about it. After checkout: the ID, then Send (Assessment page, screens S8 and S9).

Mobile and build notes

  • Fields are 50px tall, full width; first and last name, expiry and code stay in pairs (each half is still 150px or more).
  • Errors appear on blur and on submit, under the field, with the core error style (R-15). Focus moves to the first error.
  • Use autocomplete tokens (email, tel, given-name, address-line1, postal-code, cc-number) and inputmode numeric for numbers.
  • Continue to ID shows the button loader (core .is-loading) while the payment provider answers; never a second click.
  • Consents are not asked again here: they were given in step 6 (U-32). Only a payment terms line from legal.
  • No countdowns, no "only today", no upsell between the form and the button (R-61).

3 · Sent and confirmed.

After Send (the last screen of step 7, U-32): says everything arrived and what comes next. The capsule progress is full. The timeline carries the one Yellow mark: the next step, the provider review. No time is promised (R-68). One shape: an outline capsule cropped by the frame edge, never under text.

Mobile and build notes

  • The capsule is the extended hub .um-cap outline (assets/patterns, built by tools/capsule_svg.py), Wash Blue at 70%.
  • Header: the account button is Outline at 44px; the logo stays taller (R-103). On mobile the header shows Account as a link; sign-in is by email link, no password (U-32).
  • Only the timeline's next step is Yellow. The page button is Dark.
  • Email address is masked on screen (d•••@example.com).

4 · Provider review (pending).

What the member sees between Send and the provider's decision: the portal home in its first state. Three phones show the states that follow: in review, the provider has a question, not prescribed.

Member portal.

His plan, his messages, his orders. Calm and private: the portal informs, it never rewards or blames (Data in the portal).

5 · Home6 · My treatment7 · Messages8 · Orders9 · Refill10 · Account11 · Help

5 · Home.

Three questions answered on arrival: what happens next, how my treatment stands, whether someone wrote to me. The message card never previews the message.

Mobile and build notes

  • Order on mobile: greeting, next step, treatment, messages, latest order. Help moves to the top bar icon.
  • One Yellow mark per screen: the next step on the timeline (Data in the portal, U-30).
  • The unread badge is Deep Teal with a Paper number, never Coral or Yellow. Screen readers hear "1 new".
  • The greeting uses the first name only. No health words on the home screen above the treatment card.

6 · My treatment.

The dose plan from the prescription, the plan reminder with its optional check, and the refill. No streaks, no scores, no "missed" days on an as-needed plan.

Mobile and build notes

  • Directions are shown exactly as the pharmacy label prints them; the portal never rewrites a dose.
  • Week dots (R-113): a marked dose fills Blue on an As-needed plan, Green on a Daily plan, with a Deep Teal check; nothing marked is Mist; today has a ring. Never red, never a product colour.
  • The reminder switch is off by default. The whole row is the 44px target; the switch itself is 52 × 32.
  • Tabs: 44px tall, the active tab underlined in Deep Teal. On 390 all three tabs fit; no horizontal scroll.

7 · Messages with the provider.

One thread per person: the provider and the care team. Attachments are chips with name and size. Notifications say only that a message arrived.

Mobile and build notes

  • Member bubbles are Deep Teal with Paper text (9.82:1); provider bubbles Mist with Deep Teal text.
  • The thread is a role="log" region so new messages are announced politely.
  • Push: off by default (Account). When on, the text is fixed: "You have a new message." Email subject: "Your provider has replied".
  • Sound: one setting for all sounds, off by default; the message sound comes from the Sound page.
  • The attach button is a 44px icon button with a visible border and a label for screen readers.

8 · Orders and tracking.

The current order with its stages, the carrier link and the plain-packaging note; past orders below with receipts. No promised delivery time.

Mobile and build notes

  • The next stage carries the one Yellow mark; finished stages are Deep Teal with a check.
  • Dates are the dates events happened. A future date shows only when the carrier provides it, labelled as the carrier's.
  • The carrier button opens the carrier site in a new tab (icon button family, R-100); it says so to screen readers.
  • Receipts are PDFs without the product name on the first line [legal to confirm].

9 · Refill request.

A short form that goes to the provider: what changed, a note, the plan and the address. Answer options use the assessment's selected style (Deep Teal border), so no Yellow appears.

Mobile and build notes

  • "Yes, something changed" opens one follow-up field below it (cross-fade 180ms), never a new page.
  • Plan change here applies to the next order only; say so in the confirmation toast.
  • After sending: a toast "Sent to your provider." and the home timeline moves the review to the next step.
  • Draft answers are kept if he leaves the page; nothing is sent until he presses the button.

10 · Account and settings.

Notifications are all off by default, with one switch for every sound. Privacy and payment sit one tap away. Personal details are masked.

Mobile and build notes

  • Switch: 52 × 32, a generic UI pill (R-105). Off: Card ground, Slate border and thumb (3:1 or more). On: Deep Teal, Paper thumb. Thumb slides 220ms.
  • Newsletter uses double opt-in (U-28): turning it on sends a confirmation email; the switch shows "Waiting for your confirmation".
  • Delete your account opens a dialog that explains what is kept by law [legal] and asks for the password again.
  • Masked values (email, phone) reveal only after a fresh sign-in.

11 · Help.

Two clear doors: the provider for treatment, support for orders and account. The emergency line sits above both. Questions open one at a time.

Mobile and build notes

  • Accordion: native details elements in one named group, so only one answer is open (R-113). Chevron turns 180° in 220ms.
  • The two help buttons differ in colour (Dark and Outline), so they never read as the same action (R-112).
  • Search covers the questions only; it never searches messages or health data.

Clinical admin.

The provider's side. Desktop first, dense, on the type scale. A monospace face would be allowed here (R-18); Inter with tabular figures is enough.

12 · Review queue13 · Assessment review14 · Prescription15 · Audit trail

12 · Review queue.

Every request waiting for a provider, oldest first. Dense, but on the type scale: rows 48px, text 14/21, labels 12/16. Flags are Wash Yellow pills with an icon; Coral stays for errors.

Tablet and build notes

  • 1024 to 1439: the Assigned column hides (shown in the row detail); the side nav stays 216px.
  • 768 to 1023: the side nav becomes a 72px icon rail with tooltips; Submitted and State merge into one column.
  • Below 768: the full queue as a list, filters as chips that wrap; a row opens the review (screen 13, mobile). Same actions and permissions as on a computer.
  • The queue shows only members in states where the signed-in provider is licensed.
  • Waiting time counts from submission; a target is shown only once clinical operations set one (R-68).

13 · Assessment review with flags.

Member summary, the answers with flags, the decision panel. Approve, ask or decline is one choice; the panel below changes with it, and there is one button. Flags never decide; the provider does.

The decision panel in its other two states (desktop size).

Ask the member a question

The case moves to "Waiting for member". The member gets a push and an email: "You have an update."

Decline

Refund follows [refund rule · operations]. The member reads the note in Messages, never in an email.

Tablet and build notes

  • 1024 to 1439: the member summary folds into a bar above the answers (name, age, state, ID check); answers and decision stay side by side.
  • 768 to 1023: one column; the decision panel follows the answers and its button sticks to the bottom of the screen.
  • Below 768: the same single column at phone size, with every action of the desktop (U-29). The member summary shrinks to one card.
  • Flags come from rules the clinical team writes; the hub never invents one (R-69). Each flag names its rule.
  • "I reviewed both flags" is required when flags exist; the button stays disabled (40% opacity) until it is checked.
  • Keyboard: J and K move between flagged answers; every shortcut also has a visible button.

14 · Prescription to the pharmacy.

After signing: what was sent, where, and whether the pharmacy received it. A failed hand-off is an error toast with a way out, never a silent wait.

Tablet and build notes

  • The status follows the pharmacy's messages; each step shows the time it happened, never a forecast.
  • Cancel prescription asks for a reason and notifies the pharmacy; it is logged in the audit trail.
  • Tablet: one column, status first.
  • The member never sees the prescription number or the pharmacy network; the portal says "At the pharmacy".

15 · Audit trail.

Every view, decision and hand-off, newest first, for one member or for everyone. Support views appear too, marked with no health data.

Tablet and build notes

  • Times are local with the zone in the export; seconds are shown because order matters.
  • Tablet: Record wraps under Action; filters wrap to two rows.
  • Export is logged as its own event.

Support.

Orders, payment and account, answered by people who never see health data. Anything clinical goes to a provider.

16 · Inbox and macros17 · Escalation

16 · Support inbox, ticket and macros.

Three panes: tickets, the open ticket, the member's order details. The macro menu is open over the composer. The PHI wall is visible, so agents know what they cannot see and why.

Tablet and build notes

  • 1024 to 1439: the member panel becomes a drawer opened from the ticket header.
  • 768 to 1023: list and ticket are separate views, like the member portal on mobile.
  • Macros fill the composer; the agent always edits before sending. Macros never contain health advice.
  • A ticket that mentions symptoms, doses or side effects shows the escalate prompt; support never answers it.

17 · Escalation to a provider.

A dialog over the ticket: the reason, a note, and exactly what the member will see. The two buttons differ in colour (R-112).

Build notes

  • Focus moves into the dialog and returns to the Escalate button when it closes; Esc cancels.
  • The escalated ticket shows in both inboxes, with one owner on each side.
  • Support never forwards the member's health words into an email.

States.

Empty, loading, error, offline and disabled, as they appear in the portal.

18 · All five states

18 · Empty, loading, error, offline, disabled.

Five states every screen needs. Each one says in words what is happening and what he can do. Loading shows the skeleton at once and the capsule loader (with the divider) after 400ms. Disabled is 40% opacity, no hover, always with the reason.

Build notes

  • Loading: skeleton at once; the loader appears only after 400ms (--motion-loader-delay) and never flashes. It is the only loop (R-53). Reduced motion: half-filled and still.
  • Error: role="alert"; the page keeps its navigation. Field errors use the core field error (Coral border and dot, text in Deep Teal).
  • Offline: role="status"; drafts are kept; sending queues and says "Send later".
  • Disabled: aria-disabled="true" (stays focusable so the reason is announced), opacity 0.4 (--opacity-disabled), no hover or lift, the control keeps its own colours (R-42).

Notification discretion.

No product names, doses or conditions in push, email subjects, previews, SMS or on the lock screen (R-108). Push, text messages and sounds are off until the member turns them on; one switch controls every sound.

EventPush (off by default)Email subjectNever
Provider messageYou have a new message.Your provider has repliedThe sender's name, the product, the text
Provider decisionYou have an update.You have an updateApproved, declined, the medicine, the dose
Order shippedYour order is on its way.Your order is on its wayThe product name, "pharmacy" in the subject
Refill dueTime to plan your next month.Time to plan your next monthThe dose, the number of tablets left
Support replyYou have a new message.We replied to your messageThe ticket topic

Accessibility.

  • Focus ring 2px Deep Teal (Paper on Teal Deep internal nav), never removed. Focus order follows the reading order; dialogs trap focus and return it.
  • Landmarks: header, nav (labelled), main. One h1 per screen; card titles are h2.
  • Current place: aria-current="page" on nav items, aria-current="step" on the timeline's next step, aria-current="date" on today.
  • Messages: role="log"; toasts role="status"; errors role="alert". New messages are announced politely, never as alerts.
  • Every chart and timeline is an ordered list or has a text equivalent; colour only repeats what the words say.
  • Contrast AA on every pair used: Deep Teal on Paper 9.82:1, Paper on Deep Teal, Slate captions on Paper; Wash Yellow and Wash Green pills carry Teal Deep text.
  • Product colours never carry text and never stand alone: the name is always written next to the mark.
  • Reduced motion: the thumb, the accordion and the loader stop; the loader shows half filled.
  • Zoom to 200% and 320px wide without sideways scroll (R-77). Tables on internal tools may scroll inside their own frame, with a visible edge.
  • Disabled controls use aria-disabled so they stay focusable and the reason next to them is read.

Files.

Product marks and the loader as standalone SVG (hex from tokens.json): mark-tadalafil.svg, mark-sildenafil.svg, mark-combo.svg, cap-loader.svg. The page is generated by assets/product-screens/page.py; styles in ps_style.css.

Questions and decisions.

All seven are answered (U-29, U-32).

#QuestionDecision
1When does the provider review: after checkout or before the price appears?Current · U-32 Decided with the assessment screens (Q99): consent, account, recommendation, checkout, ID, then Send. The provider reviews after Send. The charge line stays [charge line · operations] (U-31).
2Recommendation wording.Current · U-29 "Matches your answers" with "Your provider makes the final decision"; never "Recommended for you" alone. Legal to confirm.
3Clinical admin and support on a phone.Current · U-29 Everything works on a phone, the same as on a computer: the queue, the review, signing and support. Signing on a phone asks for [a fresh sign-in · engineering].
4Disabled buttons.Current · U-29 40% opacity with the button's own colours (R-42, token --opacity-disabled).
5Clinical flags: Wash Yellow pill with an icon, or Coral?Current · U-29 Wash Yellow. Coral stays for errors and out-of-range results (R-15).
6Portal logo.Current · U-29 Horizontal 30px in the side nav, Primary seal 40px in the mobile top bar, for app screens. The website header rule R-103 stays for the website.
7The UI icons used here.They come from the UI set on Icons (assets/icons/ui/); its status lives there.
